title: Quantum vs Classical Final Consolidated Comparison

Q1_continual_quantum_vs_classical.question: Does continual quantum personalization outperform continual classical?
Q1_continual_quantum_vs_classical.finding: Quantum classifiers (Fixed and Trainable) achieve significantly higher Macro-F1 (~0.118 vs 0.101) and drastically lower FER (~0.17 vs 0.44), but suffer severe emergency recall deficits (5.1%-5.8% vs 16.2%), causing safety vetos in clinical deployment.

Q2_adaptive_quantum_vs_fixed_quantum.question: Does adaptive quantum representation outperform fixed quantum?
Q2_adaptive_quantum_vs_fixed_quantum.finding: Trainable quantum representation does not produce a statistically significant Macro-F1 improvement over fixed quantum kernel (0.1187 vs 0.1180, p_adj=0.061). Emergency recall remains statistically unchanged (5.81% vs 5.12%, p_adj=0.559).

Q3_hybrid_fusion_vs_standalone.question: Does hybrid fusion outperform both classical and quantum standalone?
Q3_hybrid_fusion_vs_standalone.finding: Hybrid fusion achieves statistically superior Macro-F1 (0.1184 vs 0.1012, p_adj=3.78e-7) and FER (0.1945 vs 0.4353) over Classical, but does not outperform Trainable Quantum on Macro-F1 (0.1184 vs 0.1187, p_adj=0.275).

Q4_safety_governance_satisfaction.question: Does any quantum approach satisfy safety governance?
Q4_safety_governance_satisfaction.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED for Pure Quantum; SUPPORTED for Classical and Governed Hybrid
Q4_safety_governance_satisfaction.finding: Pure quantum models fail the clinical Emergency Recall safety gate due to persistent collapse onto General Speech. Hybrid fusion passes Phase 7.6 validation gate in 52/60 cells under calibrated decision thresholds.

overall_scientific_conclusion: CASE B - NO STATISTICALLY SUPPORTED QUANTUM ADVANTAGE (CONFIRMED AND REINFORCED ACROSS CONTINUAL LEARNING)
deployment_recommendation: Continual Classical Adapter remains the safest deployable architecture for atypical emergency speech recognition due to superior emergency recall (16.20%). Governed Hybrid is promising for false-alarm suppression in high-resource tiers.
